{{Short description|Scottish mathematician (1923–1999)}}
{{Use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=April 2022}}
'''Elizabeth Adam McHarg''' (22 April 1923 – 29 April 1999){{r|herald}} was a Scottish mathematician who, in 1965, became the first female president of the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]].{{r|emspres|3pres}}

==Education==
McHarg studied at the [[High School of Glasgow|Glasgow High School for Girls]] and then at the [[University of Glasgow]], earning a master's degree with first-class honours in mathematics and natural philosophy in 1943. The university awarded her the Thomas Logan Medal and a George A. Clark scholarship, funding her as a researcher at [[Girton College, Cambridge]].{{r|herald}} At Girton, she studied [[Differential equation|nonlinear partial differential equation]]s with [[Mary Cartwright]] and completed her Ph.D. in 1948.{{r|herald|celebratio}}

==Career and contributions==
McHarg returned to the University of Glasgow as a lecturer in 1948. There, she became an expert in [[special functions]].{{r|herald}} She also translated the text ''Differential Equations'' by [[Francesco Tricomi]] from [[Italian language|Italian]] into English; her translation was published in 1961 by Hafner and republished in 2012 by Dover Publications.{{r|herald|kazarinoff}}
